shipped_rows.title_o: Physical Order Produces Healthy Choices, Generosity, and Conventionality, Whereas Disorder Produces Creativity

blind_target.title: Environmental disorder leads to self-regulatory failure.
blind_target.evidence_quote: We also compared the effect of experimental conditions only considering the rotations that most closely resembled the task order in Vohs et al. (2013) and Chae and Zhu (2014) .
blind_target.outcome_quote: Results in our study indicated that working at a messy desk did not result in significantly and reliably different creativity or executive functioning performance.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The original disorder effect was not found. The authors report no creativity or executive functioning differences, and explicitly compare the designs and discrepant results to this original.

luna_triage.reason: The study measured executive functioning under orderly versus disorderly workspaces. In Discussion it directly compares its results and design with Chae and Zhu’s reported disorder effects on Stroop executive functioning and perseverance. That is an empirical retest of a specific Chae and Zhu finding. Shipped row 2478 is Vohs et al. (2013), the separate creativity original. No prior adjudication exists.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Similarly, we noted certain differences between our study and the one by Chae and Zhu (2014) , who reported an effect of disorder on executive functioning (overall RT at the Stroop task) and perseverance (time spent working on an unsolvable puzzle).
